skill.name: git-pushing
skill.description: Automates a Git workflow that stages all changes, creates a conventional commit, detects the active branch, and pushes it to origin.
skill.summary: Stage, commit, and push the active Git branch with a conventional message.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: No evidence of malicious code or prompt injection was found. The main risk is the intended Bash workflow that stages every change, commits, and pushes to origin. Several markdown and HTTP-library alerts are false positives.

remediation.issue: The script stages all changes and pushes immediately.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required review step that shows git status and a diff summary before committing.

remediation.issue: The workflow tells assistants to always use the script.
remediation.suggestion: Permit manual safety checks and require explicit user confirmation before running the script.

remediation.issue: The default commit message can create vague project history.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for or generate a specific conventional commit message before committing.

The markdown block instructs the assistant to run the Bash script. That script performs external Git commands with repository-wide effects.
This range is markdown fence syntax and surrounding prose, not Ruby backtick execution. The actual shell invocation is covered by adjacent findings.
The markdown block documents running the Bash script with a custom commit message. The script then stages, commits, and pushes the active branch.
Line 3 is front matter text describing Git push behavior and contains no Python HTTP library use. No HTTP client code appears at this location.

semantic_findings.title: Unreviewed Repository Push Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill says it should automatically activate for push requests and always use the script. The script stages all changes, commits them, and pushes the active branch, which can publish unintended files without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The trigger rules and script behavior directly show automatic activation plus git add, commit, and push. This is useful automation but creates clear publication risk.

content.value_statement: Manual Git publishing can miss staging, commit, or upstream steps. This skill runs a focused workflow for conventional commits and branch pushes.
actual_capabilities: Stages all files in the current repository with git add.
Creates a Git commit with a supplied or default conventional message.
Detects the current branch before publishing.
Pushes the branch to the origin remote with upstream tracking.
Provides activation guidance for commit-and-push requests.
limitations: It does not inspect diffs or detect secrets before staging changes.
It assumes the repository has a configured origin remote.
It does not handle merge conflicts, rejected pushes, or branch protection rules.
It commits all tracked and untracked changes in the working tree.

use_cases.title: Finish a Solo Feature
use_cases.description: Stage completed work, create a conventional commit, and push the active branch for backup or review.

use_cases.title: Publish an AI-Assisted Change
use_cases.description: Send reviewed assistant changes to the remote repository with a consistent commit message.

use_cases.title: Share a Team Update
use_cases.description: Push a finished branch so teammates can review, test, or continue the work.

prompt_templates.title: Commit And Push Current Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit and push my current changes with a clear conventional commit message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for publishing finished local changes.

prompt_templates.title: Use A Specific Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Commit and push these changes with the message: feat: add checkout validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer workflow when the commit message is already chosen.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare A Branch Push
prompt_templates.prompt: Stage all repository changes, create a conventional commit, and push the active branch to origin with upstream tracking.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for a new branch that needs upstream tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Publish After Review
prompt_templates.prompt: After I review the diff and confirm, run the Git pushing workflow with a conventional message that summarizes the changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow that adds review before publishing.

output_examples.output: The assistant stages the repository, creates a conventional commit, pushes the current branch to origin, and reports success or any Git error.

output_examples.input: Push with message feat: improve onboarding.
output_examples.output: The assistant uses the requested message, publishes the active branch with upstream tracking, and confirms the branch name.
The assistant follows the push workflow for the configured origin remote and reports whether the push completed.

best_practices: Review Git status and diff before asking the assistant to push.
Provide the exact conventional commit message when release notes matter.
Confirm that the remote branch and repository are correct before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill when unreviewed secrets or private files may be staged.
Do not run it in repositories with unresolved merge conflicts.
Do not rely on the default commit message for meaningful project history.

faq.question: Does it push to GitHub?
faq.answer: It pushes to the configured origin remote, which may be GitHub or another Git host.

faq.question: Does it review code before committing?
faq.answer: No. Review the diff before using the workflow if correctness or privacy matters.

faq.question: Can I provide my own commit message?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts a custom conventional commit message as its first argument.

faq.question: What happens if no message is provided?
faq.answer: The script uses a default conventional commit message for the commit.

faq.question: Does it set upstream tracking?
faq.answer: Yes. The push command sets upstream tracking for the active branch on origin.

faq.question: Will it handle failed pushes?
faq.answer: It stops on errors, but it does not resolve conflicts, authentication failures, or branch protection rules.
